topic_summary: Analysis of the personhood boundary in abortion law, examining how different legal and philosophical traditions define when moral and legal status begins, and how these definitions structure rights, obligations, and permissible state action. The boundary determines victim sets, rights-holders, and the legitimacy of state intervention.

key_entities: State (enforcement authority claiming legitimacy to regulate)
Religious institutions (interpretive authorities for natural law traditions)
key_tensions: Fetal moral status vs maternal autonomy (zero-sum rights allocation)
State police power vs individual liberty (scope of legitimate regulation)
Fixed textual interpretation vs evolving social consensus (constitutional stability vs adaptation)
key_mechanisms: Viability doctrine (Roe framework linking permissible regulation to fetal development stage)
Undue burden test (Casey standard for evaluating regulation severity)
key_absences: Non-Western legal traditions' personhood frameworks (Islamic fiqh, Confucian, Indigenous)
Disability rights perspective on selective termination
Economic coercion dynamics (poverty as constraint on choice)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood boundary — the point at which moral and legal status begins — is a shared commitment that all parties argue about but read differently
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Interpretive legitimacy derives from constitutional text (originalism), moral philosophy (natural law), medical expertise (viability), or democratic process (popular sovereignty)

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at conception (fertilization)
readings.authority_grounding: Natural law / religious doctrine (Catholic, evangelical Protestant traditions)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus enters victim set at conception; abortion becomes homicide-equivalent; high suppression of alternative readings; state acquires duty to prohibit

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at viability (capacity for independent life outside womb)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Pre-viability: maternal autonomy dominates; post-viability: state interest permits regulation; boundary shifts with medical technology

readings.commitment: Moral and legal personhood begins at birth (complete separation from maternal body)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Fetus never enters victim set; pregnant person sole rights-holder; no state interest in fetal protection pre-birth

readings.commitment: Moral status increases gradually across gestation; no single bright-line boundary
readings.expected_structural_delta: Sliding scale of state interest; trimester-based or developmental-milestone frameworks; permits compromise positions

axiom_contradictions.basis: Conception reading requires accepting fetal moral status as equivalent to born persons (abortion = homicide); birth reading requires accepting that location relative to maternal body determines moral status (pre-birth fetus has no independent moral claims). No single coherent framework holds both: one must either accept fetal personhood or deny it.

Conception reading grounds personhood in biological origin (intrinsic property present from fertilization); viability reading grounds personhood in technological capacity for independence (extrinsic property dependent on medical context). No framework coherently holds both: personhood is either intrinsic to the organism or contingent on external support capacity.

omegas.description: Viability reading creates moving target: as NICU technology improves, the boundary shifts earlier in gestation. Is this a feature (adaptive law) or a bug (unstable rights)? Ectogenesis may collapse viability reading entirely.

Analysis limited to Western legal-philosophical traditions. Islamic fiqh (ensoulment at 120 days), Confucian relational personhood, and Indigenous frameworks offer structurally distinct readings but exceed model domain competence.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + F34 epistemic trespass boundary

omegas.description: Conception and birth readings hold mutually exclusive axioms yet coexist in federal system. Does this represent licensed plurality (federalism as conflict-management) or deferred civil conflict? Post-Dobbs interstate enforcement attempts test this boundary.

Gradualist reading avoids bright-line problems but lacks principled stopping point. At what developmental stage does state interest become compelling? Trimester framework was judicial compromise, not philosophical derivation.
